summary.title: Callie
summary.pov: Third Person Limited (focalized through Callie). The narrative voice remains close to her sensory experience and internal logic but retains a slight distance for tactical description.
summary.synopsis: The group sets up an ambush against hounds using a 'hook' lure. When the plan fails because the hounds avoid light rather than seeking it, Callie improvises by becoming the new wall on the opposite side of the wagon to redirect the attack. The confrontation results in three hounds being killed (two by Katori/Ines, one by Duchess), but a fourth bypasses them to threaten Callie's mother before being destroyed. The chapter ends with the collection of 'Flask' ash and the death of Callie's mother.
summary.openingState: Grey light; high tension; stillness after night activity. No food eaten. Pell is anxious (fidgeting with Duchess). Ines explains the hounds' ritualistic counting behavior via tracks.
turningPoints: Callie realizes the 'hook' acts as a wall, not a lure; the hounds move to the opposite side of camp from light sources.
Callie abandons her position at the hook and runs across the wagon bed (despite injury) to become the new focal point on the east.
The fourth hound bypasses the main engagement to attack the front/mother; Duchess intervenes with a kick.
summary.closingState: Midnight. Total darkness except for distant artificial light. Callie is kneeling by her dying mother, counting time as she passes away. The group has four Flasks of ash and one lame horse.

characters.name: Callie
characters.vocalBehavior: Internal monologue is analytical but physically constrained by pain. Dialogue becomes urgent, flat, or small when realizing errors; screams only in immediate crisis. Rhythm shifts from measured planning to frantic physical exertion (running with broken ribs) to quiet counting at the end.

locations: East side of wagon bed (mother's position/Callie's new stand)
Road seam where hook was set
terms: Hounds: Four-legged, ash-colored predators that count and choose a 'side' to attack.
Hook: A steel device with worked power (light) used as bait/wall.
Flask: The solidified remains of hounds; valuable resource collected from grey ash.
Ward/Ember: Callie's ability to become an impassable wall when lit by the hook or her own presence.
summary.actionCadence: Slow, observational opening (tracking) -> Tense waiting period -> Sudden, silent movement of hounds -> Rapid, chaotic combat sequence with specific focus on soundlessness and physical impact -> Immediate aftermath (calm collection).
summary.emotionalRegister: Restraint is paramount. Fear is suppressed by duty until the final moments where grief manifests as a mechanical counting ritual rather than weeping.
narrationRisks: The description of Callie running with 'two ribs gone' must not sound like heroic exertion; it should feel physically painful and labored, emphasizing her limited breath capacity.
The hounds' movement is described as silent ('no bark', 'no scrabble'). Narrator must avoid adding auditory cues that don't exist in the text (e.g., no growls or heavy breathing from beasts).
Callie's realization of the hook being a wall needs to be delivered with sudden clarity, not melodramatic epiphany. The line 'It's not a lure' should feel small and flat.
The death scene requires absolute stillness in the narration; do not rush the counting sequence (60-142).
Pell's dialogue regarding Duchess must be delivered with quiet reverence, avoiding sentimentality.
carryForward: Callie is physically injured and emotionally devastated by her mother's death.
The group has four Flasks of ash but no way to move the wagon due to the horse's injury (Duchess).
Pell has recorded Duchess as a hero, altering his usual ledger protocol.
